title: Choosing a Study Partner
script: Alya: [hopeful] Mariam, would you like to study together for the language test next month?
Mariam: [careful] Maybe. I enjoy studying with friends, but our last group talked more than it studied.
Alya: I remember. Six people were too many, and nobody had a clear plan.
Mariam: What kind of study session are you suggesting this time?
Alya: [practical] Only the two of us, twice a week, for forty-five minutes after work.
Mariam: That sounds realistic. What would we do during those forty-five minutes?
Alya: For the first ten minutes, we can review vocabulary and test each other without looking at notes.
Mariam: Then perhaps we could practice one listening exercise and compare our answers.
Alya: [agreeing] Good idea. We should explain why we chose each answer, not only check the answer key.
Mariam: I also need speaking practice. Could we finish with a short role-play each time?
Alya: [enthusiastic] Yes. We can use situations from the course, such as visiting a clinic or asking for directions.
Mariam: Where should we meet? The café near work is convenient, but the music is sometimes loud.
Alya: The public library has a small discussion room. We can reserve it online for free.
Mariam: [relieved] Perfect. I want us to agree on one more thing: if either person is tired, we still begin on time.
Alya: Agreed, but we can choose a lighter activity instead of canceling the whole session.
Mariam: I like that. A short useful meeting is better than waiting for a perfect evening.
Alya: Shall we try Tuesday and Thursday for two weeks, then review whether it helps?
Mariam: Yes. I will reserve Tuesday's room, and you can choose our first listening exercise.
Alya: [confident] Deal. I feel calmer already because the plan is specific.
Mariam: Me too. A good study partner is helpful, but a clear routine makes the partnership work.

quiz.question: Why was the last study group ineffective?
options: It was too large and lacked a plan
quiz.explanation: Six people talked without following a clear plan.

quiz.question: How often will Alya and Mariam meet?
quiz.explanation: They plan two sessions each week.

quiz.question: What will they do after vocabulary review?
quiz.explanation: Listening practice follows the opening vocabulary review.

quiz.question: Where will they study?
quiz.explanation: They choose a free discussion room at the library.

quiz.question: What will happen after two weeks?
options: They will take the final test
They will review whether the plan helps
quiz.explanation: The first two weeks are a trial of their routine.

quiz.question: Why do they choose only two people?
options: The last group was too large
quiz.explanation: A smaller group will be easier to organize and focus.

quiz.question: What does “role-play” mean here?
options: Practice a situation by acting it out
quiz.explanation: They will act through situations such as a clinic visit.

quiz.question: Why do they explain their listening answers?
options: Reasons show how they understood the audio
The test is only about grammar
quiz.explanation: They want to learn from the thinking, not only check a letter.

quiz.question: What will they do when tired?
options: Choose an easier activity and still meet
quiz.explanation: A lighter session keeps the routine without demanding perfect energy.

quiz.question: Why does the plan make them calmer?
options: The time, place, and tasks are clear
quiz.explanation: Specific decisions reduce uncertainty about studying.
